# claude's surface, read off the binary

Everything the installed `claude` will say about itself, captured by
`scripts/claude-surface.sh` and regenerated on demand by
`.github/workflows/claude-surface.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` only, no
schedule, no credential). It is `docs/agy-surface.md` and
`docs/codex-surface.md`'s counterpart for the third CLI `pkg/agent`
drives, and it exists for one question neither of those can answer: is the
argv `pkg/agent/claude` builds argv this claude parses?

There are two of them, and they were derived from each other by hand.
`claude -p --tools "" --mcp-config <file> --strict-mcp-config
--allowedTools <names> --output-format stream-json --verbose` is the
unattended run (`claude.go`, plus `--max-turns` and `--resume` from
`retry.go`), and the same thing minus print mode and the two flags that
make print mode parseable is the interactive session (`terminal.go`).
Until this capture existed, neither had been checked against a binary --
and that same derivation is what put `codex exec`'s `--skip-git-repo-check`
on an interactive codex session, where the first thing whoever opened it
saw was `error: unexpected argument`.

Read it as evidence rather than as documentation: every section below is a
command and its output, the commands that failed included. A probe that
stopped answering is itself a finding.

Claude is pinned in the Dockerfile. This capture records the same version,
and `pkg/agent/claude/surface_capture_test.go` fails when the pin changes
until the surface is regenerated and reviewed.

## The binary

``````console
$ claude --version
2.1.286 (Claude Code)
``````

``````console
path   /opt/claude/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.286
size   241667256 bytes
sha256 fe503f65c6289d59c23e5b21ae44f03583f997dd33a2cbfc75ab4f96fb8fc73f
``````

How the image gets its claude, against the claude that answered here:

``````console
installed by the Dockerfile   pinned: ARG CLAUDE_CLI_VERSION=2.1.286
captured here                 2.1.286 (Claude Code)
``````

``````console
      Prefix for auto-generated Remote Control session names (default: hostname)

                                        conversation and reuse it verbatim on
                                        every request and resume. on (the
                                        default): the prompt is rendered on the
                                        conversation's first request — a
                                        --system-prompt or

                                        resume sends the record as-is, even when
                                        a later launch passes different text,

  --verbose                             Override verbose mode setting from
                                        config
  -v, --version                         Output the version number
  -w, --worktree [name]                 Create a new git worktree for this
                                        session (optionally specify a name)

Commands:
  agents [options]                      Manage background agents

  logs <id>                             Print a background session's recent

  mcp                                   Configure and manage MCP servers
  plugin|plugins                        Manage Claude Code plugins
  project                               Manage Claude Code project state
  respawn [options] [id]                Restart a background session, or all of

  rm <id>                               Delete a background session, and its

  setup-token                           Set up a long-lived authentication token

  stop|kill <id>                        Stop a background session. Its

  ultrareview [options] [target]        Run a cloud-hosted multi-agent code
                                        review of the current branch (or a PR
                                        number / base branch) and print the

  update|upgrade                        Check for updates and install if
``````

### `claude agents`

``````console
$ claude agents --help
Usage: claude agents [options]

Manage background agents

Options:
  --add-dir <directory>                 Additional directory to allow tool
                                        access to in dispatched sessions
                                        (repeatable)
  --agent <agent>                       Default agent for sessions dispatched
                                        from agent view. Overrides the 'agent'
                                        setting.
  --all                                 With --json: also include completed
                                        background sessions
  --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions  Make bypass-permissions mode available
                                        to dispatched sessions without
                                        defaulting to it
  --cwd <path>                          Show only background sessions started
                                        under <path>
  --dangerously-skip-permissions        Alias for --permission-mode
                                        bypassPermissions
  --effort <level>                      Default effort level for sessions
                                        dispatched from agent view
  -h, --help                            Display help for command
  --json                                Print active sessions (interactive and
                                        background) as a JSON array and exit
                                        (for scripting; does not require a TTY)
  --mcp-config <config>                 MCP server configuration to apply to
                                        dispatched sessions (repeatable)
  --model <model>                       Default model for sessions dispatched
                                        from agent view
  --permission-mode <mode>              Default permission mode for sessions
                                        dispatched from agent view
  --plugin-dir <path>                   Load plugins from specified directory
                                        for the agent view and dispatched
                                        sessions; a folder of plugins loads each
                                        child (repeatable)
  --restricted                          Start dispatched sessions in restricted
                                        mode
  --setting-sources <sources>           Comma-separated list of setting sources
                                        to load (user, project, local).
  --settings <file-or-json>             Settings file or JSON string to apply to
                                        the agent view and dispatched sessions
  --strict-mcp-config                   Only use MCP servers from --mcp-config
                                        in dispatched sessions
``````

## Where each flag lives

Every long flag `claude --help` listed, sorted. This is the set the two argv below are drawn from, and a flag that leaves it is a flag that has been renamed or withdrawn -- which is a diff on this list rather than a surprise in production.

``````console
$ the long flags claude --help lists
``````

Two things this list is not.

It is not the whole flag set. `--max-turns`, which `retry.go` passes on every capped attempt, is nowhere in it, and the probe table below finds this claude accepting it all the same: a flag can be undocumented and live. That is the argument for probing rather than reading.

And it is not a flag set the subcommands share. `claude` and `claude mcp list` are separate commander commands, the way `codex` and `codex exec` are, and the top-level options do not reach the subcommand:

``````console
$ claude mcp list --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config
error: unknown option '--mcp-config'
[exit 1]
``````

Nothing in this repository runs `claude mcp` -- `pkg/agent/claude` passes `--mcp-config` to the session and the run themselves -- so that refusal is here as the shape of the answer, not as a bug. It is what `--skip-git-repo-check` looked like on codex.

## The argv grain builds

The listing above is what claude says. This section is what it does, asked one flag at a time and in the exact argv `pkg/agent/claude` builds: `print` is `claude -p <flag>`, the unattended run's shape (`Run`, `attemptArgs`), and `session` is `claude <flag>`, the shape `TerminalCommand` hands `pkg/console`.

Every probe here is run for real, with stdin closed and both `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` removed from the environment. Appending `--help` -- which is how the codex capture parses without running -- proves nothing against claude: commander acts on `--help` the moment it reaches it, so `claude --no-such-flag --help` exits 0 and prints the help. Running it instead is safe because claude will not start a turn without a prompt: what an accepted argv gets is `Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument`, which is the parser having read every flag and then found nothing to do. No probe in this document starts a model turn.

`accepted` therefore means the flag is spelled and positioned correctly, and nothing more. It is not a claim about the value, and not a claim that the flag does anything here: claude documents half a dozen options as "only works with --print" and takes them silently without it.

It is also why the `session` rows come back quoting print mode. A probe's stdout is a pipe, and claude reads a redirected stdout as print mode whatever else is on the command line -- so what these rows measure is the parser, which is the same parser either way. Whether the *interactive* half of the binary takes the same argv is a question only a pty can answer, and "Interactive mode" below is where it is asked.

This list is the one place in this document that names flags rather than discovering them, and `pkg/agent/claude/surface_capture_test.go` is what keeps it honest: a flag that package passes and this script does not probe fails that test rather than going unmeasured.

``````console
$ does this claude accept the flag in that argv
accepted  print    --tools                Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --mcp-config           Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --strict-mcp-config    Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --allowedTools         Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --output-format        Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --verbose              Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --model                Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --max-turns            Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  print    --resume               No conversation found with session ID: $UUID
accepted  session  --tools                Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --mcp-config           Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --strict-mcp-config    Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --allowedTools         Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --output-format        Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --verbose              Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --model                Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --max-turns            Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  session  --resume               No conversation found with session ID: $UUID
``````

And the argv whole, since a flag set that parses one flag at a time can still be refused together -- which matters more here than it did for codex, because three of these options are variadic (`--tools <tools...>`, `--mcp-config <configs...>`, `--allowedTools <tools...>`) and a variadic option swallows everything after it that does not start with a dash.

``````console
$ does this claude accept the whole command line
accepted  claude -p --tools "" --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__grain-sandbox__run_command --output-format stream-json --verbose --model claude-sonnet-5
          the unattended run: Run's own argv -- Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
accepted  claude -p --tools "" --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__grain-sandbox__run_command --output-format stream-json --verbose --model claude-sonnet-5 --max-turns 12 --resume $UUID
          the same, as attemptArgs builds a capped retry that resumes -- No conversation found with session ID: $UUID
accepted  claude --tools "" --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__grain-sandbox__run_command --model claude-sonnet-5
          the session: TerminalCommand -- Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
``````

That last row is the one worth reading twice. The prompt of a real run travels on stdin rather than in argv (`Run`, deliberately: untrusted issue content must never be a `ps`-visible argument), and this document is the reason to keep it that way -- a positional argument after `--mcp-config <file>` is not a prompt to claude, it is a second config file:

``````console
$ claude -p --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json "a prompt in argv rather than on stdin"
Error: Invalid MCP configuration:
MCP config file not found: $PROBE/plain-1/a prompt in argv rather than on stdin
[exit 1]
``````

## Interactive mode

What `claude` does with no `-p` at all, which is what `TerminalCommand` runs. `pkg/console` starts it with no working directory of its own (`terminal.go` sets no `Dir`), so on a deployed host it opens wherever the daemon happens to be -- neither a checkout nor anywhere the run's own files are.

First, without a terminal. This is not an interactive claude at all, and that is the finding: with stdout redirected, claude reads its own command line as print mode whatever else is on it.

``````console
$ claude --tools "" --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__grain-sandbox__run_command --model claude-sonnet-5, stdout redirected
Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
[exit 1]
``````

The same command inside a git repository, so that the message above can be read for what it is not about -- unlike codex, claude has no repository check to skip and no `--skip-git-repo-check` to skip it with:

``````console
$ claude --tools "" --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__grain-sandbox__run_command --model claude-sonnet-5, in a git repository
Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
[exit 1]
``````

So the interactive half of this binary only exists on a pty. Below is exactly the argv `TerminalCommand` returns, started on one, in a HOME whose first-run questions have been answered (a fresh HOME draws the theme picker and nothing else). No credential is planted: an unauthenticated claude gets as far as the screen this section is about either way. A word list rather than a screen, for the reason `tui_fragments` gives in the script.

### The session argv, on a pty

``````console
$ claude --tools "" --mcp-config $PROBE/config-1/mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__grain-sandbox__run_command --model claude-sonnet-5, on a pty
``````

Two things are in that list and both matter. There is no `error:` line, which is this document's whole question answered for the half of it a test cannot reach: the session argv is argv the interactive claude parses too. And there is a workspace-trust question -- claude asks whoever opened the session whether it may read the directory it started in, before anything else happens.

Nothing on that command line pre-empts that question, and nothing in `pkg/agent/claude` tries to. `-p` does (claude's own `--print` help: "The workspace trust dialog is skipped when Claude is run in non-interactive mode"), which is why an unattended run never sees it and a session always does.

## What it loads out of the config grain writes

A session and an unattended run of the same task are handed the same `--mcp-config` file, written by `writeMCPConfig` from `mcpConfigJSON`, and everything a run can reach is in it: `--tools ""` empties claude's native roster, `--strict-mcp-config` ignores every other MCP configuration, and `--allowedTools` filters what is left. The file, as that function builds it (copied into this script, and diffable against it by eye):

``````json
{"mcpServers":{"grain":{"command":"/bin/true","args":["mcpserver","-sandbox","$PROBE/sandbox"]}}}
``````

What claude does with a `--mcp-config` it cannot read, which is the failure mode a wrong path in this repository would produce -- loud, and before any turn:

``````console
$ claude -p --mcp-config $PROBE/no-such-config.json --strict-mcp-config
Error: Invalid MCP configuration:
MCP config file not found: $PROBE/no-such-config.json
[exit 1]
``````

## The keys, out of the string table

claude ships as one ~200MB file with its whole JavaScript bundle inside it, so every flag name it accepts, every environment variable it reads and every JSON key it looks for is in there as a literal. These are the names `pkg/agent/claude` depends on and cannot check any other way -- the environment variables especially, since none of them appears in `--help`. A name that stops appearing here is a name a new claude has renamed, and an environment variable set under a renamed name is silently no setting at all.

``````console
$ each name pkg/agent/claude depends on, in the binary's own strings
present                  MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT
present                  CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
present                  CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY
present                  strict-mcp-config
present                  allowedTools
present                  mcp-config
present                  max-turns
present                  output-format
present                  stream-json
present                  mcpServers
``````

And what claude itself will say about the roster `--tools` empties, which is the one argument in this repository whose behaviour no probe here can demonstrate without a model turn. A window around the match rather than a sentence, since a bundle has no separators between its literals:

``````console
$ strings -n 4 claude | grep -aoE '.{0,60}disable all tools.{0,60}'
he list of available tools from the built-in set. Use "" to disable all tools, "default" to use all tools, or specify tool names (e.g. "B
``````
